caption_link.limitation: The source provides matching numeric IDs only. It does not provide an original post URL, date, media link, or an explicit asset-to-caption key.

inspection.evidence_scope: Source-bound start, material-intermediate, and near-complete frames were extracted from the original local GIF and visually inspected; metadata came from that same source file.

motion_sampling.method: Three source-bound frame samples extracted from the original local GIF for review; no derivative was added to the corpus.
motion_sampling.limitation: The near-end sample is in a visibly partial reset/fade. Three sampled frames establish the observed state change, not a frame-by-frame reconstruction of timing or platform playback.

visual_anatomy.title: A short instructional headline uses an underlined lead-in and one lavender rough-display outcome word, followed by a one-sentence three-kind distinction.
visual_anatomy.layout: A three-column comparison table fills the canvas. Each column has a category header, an upper time-and-success curve, and aligned rows for shelf life, engagement ranges, content traits, how-to-create guidance, best fit, and business effects.
visual_anatomy.reading_order: Headline and framing → category headers → animated trajectory curves → scan each repeated row across the three columns.
visual_anatomy.typography: Light sans title with rough-display emphasis; bold compact row labels; small list text, numerical ranges, and pill-like recommendations inside the table.
visual_anatomy.colour: Pink, aqua, and lavender column identities repeat in the headers, graph areas, recommendation pills, and bottom effect cells against white table cells.
visual_anatomy.surface: Thin black grid, flat tinted bands, hand-drawn underline, line/area curves, rounded outline pills, and very restrained shadowing.
visual_anatomy.modules: One three-way comparison matrix with three curve slots and seven repeated qualitative/quantitative comparison rows.
visual_anatomy.density: High: a reader can use it as an index because every category holds the same question in the same place.

motion.observed_state_change: The opening sample shows the comparison grid and partially empty category headers/graph space. The intermediate sample has revealed category names, an early spike curve, a middle hump, and coloured row fills; by the near-end sample the third long-tail curve and the full category comparison are visible before reset.
motion.motion_job: Use temporal curve drawing to make the claimed difference in lifespan/trajectory immediately legible before the reader works through the dense comparison rows.
motion.limitation: The near-end sample is in a visibly partial reset/fade. Three sampled frames establish the observed state change, not a frame-by-frame reconstruction of timing or platform playback.

transferable_mechanism.reader_job: Compare several types of an outcome by both their temporal pattern and the practical decisions associated with each type.
transferable_mechanism.argument_shape: Shared-metric category comparison with a time-shape row and aligned operational rows.
transferable_mechanism.mechanism: Give every category a common chart frame for the one variable that changes over time, then align the same practical questions beneath it so the reader can compare trade-offs without switching visual systems.
transferable_mechanism.use_condition: Use only when categories share defensible dimensions and the charted quantities, rates, and business implications are traceable. Do not draw attractive curves to substitute for data.

anti_copy_boundary: Do not reuse the virality subject, three category names, exact engagement ranges, curve shapes, table rows, title wording, rough-display tag, pastel columns, or claim about business results.

claim_boundary.note: No matching caption was supplied. The asset presents specific engagement ranges, behavioural descriptions, and commercial implications without source, method, scope, or independent verification.
